name: Thiel-Behnke Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Thiel-Behnke Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic honeycomb-shaped subepithelial corneal opacities on slit-lamp examination
Histopathological identification of curly collagen deposits in Bowman's layer
Detection of pathogenic mutation in the TGFBI gene, commonly R555Q variant
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic honeycomb corneal opacities plus either histopathological confirmation or identification of TGFBI mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from Reis-Bücklers corneal dystrophy is critical due to overlapping features.

laboratory: Histopathology showing curly collagen deposits in Bowman's layer
Corneal epithelial cell irregularities on cytology
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing honeycomb-shaped subepithelial opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing Bowman's layer abnormalities
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Reis-Bücklers dystrophy shows more geographic opacities and earlier onset
Histopathology reveals rod-shaped deposits rather than curly collagen
TGFBI mutation R555W instead of R555Q
Lattice dystrophy characterized by amyloid deposits forming lattice lines
Slit-lamp shows branching refractile lines rather than honeycomb pattern

redFlags: Rapid progression of corneal opacities with vision loss
Recurrent severe corneal erosions unresponsive to standard therapy
Signs of secondary infection or corneal ulceration
references: Weiss JS, Møller HU, Lisch W, et al. The IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies–edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
Klintworth GK. Corneal dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:7.
